name: CO2 to urea and polymers
principle: Urea plants consume CO2 from ammonia production as a feedstock, and Covestro makes CO2-based polyether carbonate polyols for polyurethane foam. Covestro's Dormagen polyols plant, started in 2016, has a capacity of 5,000 t/yr and supports foams that contain about 20% CO2.

source.note: European Rubber Journal, Covestro starts CO2-based polyols plant, 20 June 2016

performance.metric: global CO2 consumption in urea manufacturing
performance.basis: Global accounting: 130 Mt CO2 used in urea, the largest single use, ahead of 70-80 Mt for enhanced oil recovery.

source.note: IEA, Putting CO2 to Use (2019), read 2026-11-17

limitations: Limited volume compared with storage (not quantified in sources read)

sources.note: European Rubber Journal, Covestro starts CO2-based polyols plant, 20 June 2016

notes: Process provenance: Documents the urea synthesis sequence - ammonia and CO2 fed to the reactor forming ammonium carbamate exothermically, then endothermic dehydration to urea and water at about 145 bar and 180 C, with CO2 stripping and a pool condenser combining condensation with part of the reactor duty.
